summaries.demographer: Alicia is a 29-year-old second-generation Colombian-American woman born in Sacramento, CA (Q01, Q85-Q89), currently residing alone in a rental apartment in the Avenues neighborhood of Chico, CA (Q08, Q11, Q58). She holds a bachelor's degree in computer science from UC Davis with a minor in studio art (Q90) and works as a computer and information research scientist earning approximately $94,000/year at a university-affiliated AI lab (Q16, Q65, Q72). Her household is a single-earner, no-children unit with one pet; she is divorced as of 2024 after a four-year marriage and is currently dating casually (Q05, Q11, Q84). Her parents — an RN mother and former truck driver / small-business owner father, both with less than a bachelor's — exemplify classic second-generation upward mobility (Q100-Q107).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Alicia displays classic long-horizon, low-impulsivity financial behavior: funded emergency reserve (~$18,000, 5-6 months of expenses), maxed Roth IRA, 8% 403(b) with employer match, and a separate brokerage 'freedom fund' earmarked for a future startup or down payment (Q61, Q62). She exhibits mild loss aversion around housing and parental-aging risks but pays credit cards in full and avoids balances (Q60, Q63, Q82). Identity-driven preferences dominate her career and consumption choices: she explicitly turned down a lucrative Chicago quant trading offer for a research path she described as the 'me choice' (Q02), and she prioritized living alone post-divorce over maximal savings (Q11). She is relatively insensitive to status consumption but will invest substantially in tooling that expands creative optionality (an $800 Wacom tablet, $300/month shared studio, conference travel) (Q56, Q59). Peer influence is high in curated in-groups — Latinx en IA, the Chico arts community, her therapist — but she actively disengaged from algorithmic platforms (Twitter, TikTok) when she judged their effect on her cognition as net-negative (Q48).
summaries.political_scientist: Alicia is a strong Democrat who self-identifies as a progressive within the party and votes in every election — general, midterm, primary, and local — using mail-in ballots and conducting extensive down-ballot research via the League of Women Voters and Ballotpedia (Q23, Q95, Q96). Her policy commitments cluster on the progressive-left of the Democratic coalition: Medicare for All, strong housing policy, tech antitrust, aggressive climate action, immigration reform, and police reform short of full abolition (Q24, Q25, Q27). Institutional trust is selective: high in scientific institutions (CDC, peer review, NSF), universities, and journalism, but low in the Catholic Church, big tech platforms, and police departments (Q42, Q47, Q25, Q20). Civic engagement is high and multi-modal — protest participation (BLM 2020 Sacramento), monthly bail-fund donations, volunteer STEM mentoring with Mujeres en STEM, arts walk committee work, and professional service through Latinx en IA paper reviews (Q17, Q21, Q26, Q29). Community attachment to Chico is strong, reinforced by chosen-family ties and post-divorce self-reinvention (Q08, Q10, Q43).
summaries.psychologist: Alicia presents as high in openness to experience — evidenced by abstract painting, generative art, speculative fiction, interdisciplinary research, and cross-cultural engagement — and moderately high in conscientiousness, though self-described as 'laid-back yet competitive' with occasional deadline slippage (Q01, Q16, seed). Her diagnosed generalized anxiety disorder (age 26) is managed competently through a multi-pronged regimen — sertraline 50 mg, biweekly therapy with Dr. Patel, yoga, caffeine-timing rules, journaling, and hiking — reflecting mature emotional regulation (Q31, Q45, Q50). Her self-concept is explicitly narrative and iterative ('life in draft form'), integrating her Colombian-American heritage, artist and scientist dual identity, and post-divorce reconstruction into a coherent identity project (Q01, Q43). Attachment style reads as earned-secure: she maintains dense, reliable relationships (Tuesday dinners with Priya for four years, near-daily contact with cousin Valentina, biweekly calls to abuela) and processed her divorce and ex-husband's remarriage with vulnerability and social support rather than avoidance (Q07, Q44). Her motivational architecture is curiosity-dominant — she names curiosity as her single highest value and explicitly ties meaning to freedom to structure her own days around creative work (Q109, Q108).
